setup: Hold a long band in front at shoulder height
Hands about shoulder width, palms down
Arms straight with a soft elbow bend
execution: Pull the band apart by moving your hands out
Bring the band toward your chest
Return slowly; keep a little tension
faults: Don't let the band snap back

notes: Check the band for nicks or tears before use; a snapping band can hit your face.
No load is logged. Make it harder with a stronger band or a narrower grip, and note which band you used.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Lighter band or wider grip
regressions.reason: Less band stretch makes each rep easier.

progressions.name: Stronger band or narrower grip
progressions.reason: More band stretch for the same movement.

progressions.name: Pause at the chest
progressions.reason: A one- or two-second squeeze adds work without a new band.

substitutions.name: Cable rear-delt fly
substitutions.reason: Same arc with stack loading you can log.

substitutions.name: Face pull
substitutions.reason: Rear delts and upper back on a rope.

substitutions.name: Reverse pec deck
substitutions.reason: Same movement seated on a machine.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at chest height, figure facing the camera holding a long flat band. The band's stretch and the hands moving out to the sides read clearly from the front.

keyPositions.label: Together
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, arms straight out in front at shoulder height, hands about shoulder width on the band, palms down, band lightly taut.

keyPositions.label: Apart
keyPositions.describe: Arms swept out to the sides like a T, band stretched across the chest, shoulder blades squeezed. Shoulders down; lower back not arched.

ikHints: Hands fixed on the band; band stays a straight line between them
emphasise: Hands move straight out to the sides
Shoulder blades squeeze at the end

uncertain.note: StrengthLog also lists the rotator cuff as primary. It is listed as secondary here (vocabulary word added 23 Oct 2026, expansion research Q1): the rear delts and upper back do the visible work.
Band tension isn't a weight, so nothing is logged (bodyweight convention, value 0), as with the band pushdown. Band colour or strength would need its own field; none exists yet.
